chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: Learning clarinet as a double
summary: Gunable insisted on clarinet, which McRae calls the natural double for any reed man; his own doubles were bass clarinet and bass sax.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Okay. Gunable also had you do some work on clarinet.
Yeah, he taught me. He had to -- see, he always said that you have to learn the clarinet because the clarinet will make you a much better saxophone player. Because clarinet was hard, you know.

And the clarinet was a very necessary instrument for any reed man. (inaudible). Eventually will have to learn the clarinet, so you might as well get on it at an early stage where you can take it along with you. With the saxophone, you know.
